# The Voyage of the Prodigal Sun

## Scripture

"In him we live and move and have our being." — Acts 17:28a (NIV)

## Reflection

Autumn's nights arrive earlier now, and if you look low along the western horizon just after sunset, you'll notice the brighter stars and constellations have crept a little further west than they were a month ago. The whole sky seems to be drifting—not because the stars are wandering away, but because our vantage point keeps changing as Earth sails around the Sun. What looks like departure is really perspective.

There's a mercy in that. Some seasons of faith feel like the light is slipping away—prayers seem to land further off, warmth of fellowship fades, and God feels lower on the horizon than He used to. But the stars haven't moved. The heavens still declare His handiwork, whether or not we can see them well from where we're standing. Paul told the Athenians that God is not far from any of us; in Him "we live and move and have our being." Our orbit may carry us through cold and shadow, but it cannot carry us outside of Him.

So if your sky feels dimmer this fall, take heart. The change is in the viewing, not in the One who set the lights in place. Hold your course. The season will turn, and the same faithful stars will rise again—because the same faithful God holds them.

## Prayer

Father, when the light seems to slip away, remind me that You have not moved. Hold me in the orbit of Your love, and teach me to trust Your faithfulness even in the dim seasons. In Jesus' name, amen.
